More and more companies are filling less in the JOLTS survey: the jobs data the Fed is watching is turning into a blind box

💡 Slightly bearish: A drop in the JOLTS participation rate → the Fed can’t see the employment picture clearly → the pace of rate cuts becomes even more unpredictable → risk assets like BTC face added pressure and volatility.

JOLTS is a monthly corporate survey conducted by the U.S. Department of Labor. It tracks job openings, hiring, and separations—one of the Fed’s core references for judging how hot or cold the job market is. Each release can make markets shiver.

The issue now is: fewer and fewer companies are willing to respond to the questionnaire. As participation keeps falling, the data no longer represents the real job market. Job openings may look like they’re declining, but it could simply be that no one is reporting—meaning employment is not necessarily cooling.

One-sentence translation: The employment map in the Fed’s hands is getting blurry. If the map is inaccurate, the car can’t drive steadily.

Market impact
Short term: The transmission path is very direct—JOLTS distortion → the Fed’s decision-making basis weakens → the market’s pricing for the timing of rate cuts swings back and forth → volatility in risk assets increases. BTC is currently around $63,054 and is almost flat over the past 24 hours, but this kind of data noise will amplify the long-vs-short game in the futures market, raising the probability of “needle-poking” moves. ETH is consolidating near $1,879 on declining volume; volume can’t pick up, so there’s no upside rebound.

Medium term: If the quality of labor data keeps deteriorating, the Fed will rely even more on inflation data to make decisions, reducing policy predictability. This isn’t a disaster for the crypto market, but it means that in the future, every jobs report’s “surprises” and “shocks” will be amplified. We’ll likely see more frequent roller-coaster行情 driven by news. For swing traders, it will get harder and harder to get a feel for the market.

My take
I’m cautiously bearish, but not by a big margin. This is more of a slow, grinding negative than a “breakdown” type. BTC is repeatedly tugging at the $63,000 round-number level. This area is originally a battlefield between bulls and bears; data uncertainty will only make the sideways chop more exhausting. If it can’t hold above the $64K round-number level, the script remains: further downside tests. ETH is weaker—$1,879 is “playing dead” on declining volume, with insufficient follow-through on upside. In this macro-noise environment, don’t expect a one-way trend. Grinding down within a range is the main theme.

Risk point: If the upcoming Non-Farm Payrolls (NFP) also reveals similar issues with statistical quality, market sentiment will get another blow.

In the first half of the year, crypto startups raised $11.2 billion, all flowing into regulated, compliant tracks

In the first half of 2026, capital flows in the crypto industry’s primary market showed a highly concentrated compliance-driven pattern. Based on a review of publicly disclosed financings by the team of Irina Heaver, founder of Dubai crypto law firm NeosLegal, crypto startups raised a total of about $11.2 billion during the period, completing 377 rounds of funding. Under the统计 methodology used, nearly all disclosed capital went to enterprises that are regulated and have licensing mechanisms, rather than to early-stage, unlicensed experimental projects that had previously been seen as industry identifiers. Some practitioners interpret this outcome as a temporary shift in capital preference, and it has also sparked discussions about whether the industry’s commercial-model focus is moving.

At the level of core facts, funding is strongly concentrated in tracks that need licenses to operate at scale. Payments and stablecoins lead with about $3.7 billion, the predicted market with roughly $2.0 billion, and crypto exchanges and trading platforms with about $1.7 billion. The predicted market figure stands out: Kalshi completed around $1 billion in funding in May, with participants including Sequoia Capital, Morgan Stanley, Ark Invest, and a16z. Polymarket received approximately $600 million in support from the Intercontinental Exchange. Related statistics also show that the predicted market completed 34 rounds of funding cumulatively within six months, indicating sustained institutional interest. The investor roster further confirms how deeply traditional finance and market infrastructure are involved: BlackRock, Apollo, HSBC, BNP Paribas, Citadel, Goldman Sachs, Nasdaq, and others appear in the investment sequence of regulated crypto companies. Mastercard acquired the stablecoin payment company BVNK for about $1.8 billion. The Abu Dhabi sovereign wealth fund ADIA participated in Canton Network’s approximately $355 million institutional blockchain financing, and also appeared alongside a16z, Apollo, HSBC, and others.

In terms of logical breakdown, licenses are being repriced from “compliance costs” to “scarce, defensible assets.” One investor noted that code can be forked in a short time, but obtaining key-jurisdiction licenses or permits often takes 18 to 24 months and requires substantial investment; what investors are effectively buying is the time window that later entrants need to catch up. Another view emphasizes that this is not merely a trade driven by a regulatory narrative, but an entry threshold based on revenue logic: regulation is the ticket, and commercial sustainability is the core of the pricing. Even the research method has limitations—undisclosed rounds are counted as zero, so the $11.2 billion figure may underestimate actual activity; and half-year data is only a snapshot—only multiple consecutive half-years can more reliably describe structural changes.

The impact path on the crypto market can be observed through capital allocation, product forms, and participant segmentation. Primary-market resources concentrating in payments, stablecoins, licensed trading, and prediction markets can help accelerate the rollout of compliant infrastructure, clearing and settlement interfaces, and institutional-grade products. At the same time, if innovations in permissionless experimentation cannot connect with mainstream primary-market capital, they may rely more on community collaboration, token mechanisms, and self-sustaining liquidity cycles in the secondary market—so funding conditions at both ends may become even more differentiated. More importantly, institutional players and retail users do not necessarily move in the same direction. As noted by exchange executives, financing data reflects institutions chasing licenses, but a large volume of small, high-frequency user trading still occurs outside the funding narrative. Demand scenarios and risk preferences are segmented.

The editorial assessment is that the materials above are better understood as a staged portrait of primary-market preference rather than a final verdict on the entire crypto ecosystem. The factual portion is clear: fundraising on the order of $11.2 billion, 377 rounds, and disclosed capital concentrated in payments stablecoins, prediction markets, and licensed trading platforms—all supported by public statistics. Speculation should be kept restrained: “the end of the unlicensed era” is a strong judgment and still depends on factors such as the scale of undisclosed financing, the activity level of open-source and experimental ecosystems, and whether real retail usage can continue to validate on the other side. For founding teams, the choice of jurisdictions and the licensing pathway may rise from being a secondary consideration to becoming a variable in the business model. For market observers, what should be watched next is whether the structure in continuous statistics is stable, how well licensed companies bring products to market, and the quality of exits—rather than the total figure from a single snapshot.

content:
上半年加密创企融资112亿尽入持牌合规赛道

2026年上半年，加密行业一级市场资金流向呈现出高度集中的合规特征。据迪拜加密法律机构NeosLegal创始人Irina Heaver团队对公开披露融资的梳理，加密初创企业在该期间合计募集约112亿美元，共完成377轮融资。统计口径下，已披露资金几乎全部进入受监管、具备许可机制的企业，而非早期被视作行业标识的无许可实验型项目。这一结果被部分从业者解读为资本偏好的阶段性切换，也引发关于行业商业模式重心迁移的讨论。

核心事实层面，资金分布高度聚焦于需要牌照才能规模化运转的赛道。支付与稳定币以约37亿美元居首，预测市场约20亿美元，加密交易所与交易平台约17亿美元。预测市场尤为醒目：Kalshi在5月完成约10亿美元融资，参与方包括红杉资本、摩根士丹利、方舟投资与a16z等；Polymarket获得洲际交易所约6亿美元支持。相关统计还显示，预测市场在六个月内累计完成34轮融资，机构兴趣具有连续性。出资名单进一步印证传统金融与市场基础设施的介入程度，贝莱德、阿波罗、汇丰、法国巴黎银行、Citadel、高盛、纳斯达克等均出现在受监管加密公司的投资序列中；万事达卡以约18亿美元收购稳定币支付公司BVNK，阿布扎比主权财富基金ADIA参与Canton Network约3.55亿美元机构区块链融资，并与a16z、阿波罗、汇丰等共同现身。

逻辑拆解上，牌照正从“合规开支”被重新定价为“稀缺且具防御性的资产”。有投资人指出，代码可在短时间内被分叉，而获得关键司法辖区执照或通行证往往需要18至24个月并伴随高额投入，投资者实际购买的是后来者追赶所需的时间窗口。另有观点强调，这并非单纯的监管叙事交易，而是收益逻辑下的入场门槛：监管是门票，商业可持续性才是定价核心。研究方法本身也有边界——未披露轮次按零计入，112亿美元可能低估真实活跃度；半年数据只是快照，连续多个半年才能更稳妥地刻画结构变化。

对加密市场的影响路径，可从资本配置、产品形态与参与者分层观察。一级市场资源向支付、稳定币、持牌交易与预测市场集中，有助于合规基础设施、清算结算接口与机构级产品加速落地；与此同时，更依赖无许可实验的创新若难以对接主流一级资本，或将更多依靠社区协作、代币机制与二级流动性自我循环，两端资金条件可能进一步分化。更关键的是机构与散户并不必然同向：有交易所管理层指出，融资数据反映机构对牌照的追逐，但大量小额、高频的用户交易仍发生在筹资叙事之外的场所，需求场景与风险偏好存在分层。

编辑判断认为，上述材料更适合被理解为一级市场偏好的阶段性画像，而不是对整个加密生态的终局宣判。事实部分清晰：112亿美元量级、377轮融资，以及披露资金向支付稳定币、预测市场、持牌交易平台集中，均有公开统计支撑。推测部分则需克制——“无许可时代结束”属于强判断，仍取决于未披露融资规模、开源与实验生态的活跃度，以及散户真实使用能否在另一侧持续验证。对创始团队而言，司法管辖区选择与持牌路径可能从附属事项上升为商业模式变量；对市场观察者而言，后续应更关注连续统计中的结构是否稳固、牌照企业的产品落地与退出质量，而非单次总量本身。

Many people understand the next market cycle as “rate cuts → BTC → ETH → a massive shanzhai surge.” The direction isn’t wrong, but the biggest misconception right now is this— the Federal Reserve hasn’t entered a new round of rate-cut trade yet.

SEC reviews 6 triple-leveraged ETFs: this time it’s not spot approval—it’s paving the way for leveraged capital

💡 Neutral: The SEC has accepted the review of six triple-leveraged commodity ETFs, including BTC and ETH. But this is only “the review has begun,” not “approved.” Even if approved, the money would go into futures first—not directly buying crypto.

What’s going on

The Cboe BZX exchange filed a rule-change document with the SEC to list six triple-leveraged commodity ETFs. The issuer is Volatility Shares. The six products are: 3x gold, 3x silver, 3x crude oil, 3x natural gas, plus 3x BTC and 3x ETH.

So-called “3x leverage” means: on the benchmark day, if the benchmark rises 1%, the fund targets a 3% rise; if it falls, the downside is amplified threefold too—pure volatility amplification. The key detail is that the BTC and ETH funds don’t hold coins directly. Their main positions are placed in CME near-month and next-month futures contracts—in essence, they leverage the futures term structure.

One-sentence translation: The SEC is putting BTC, ETH, gold, and crude oil in the same box as commodities for review. A leveraged crypto ETF has entered the regulatory process, but it’s still several hurdles away from being truly listed.

Impact on the market

- Short term: Neutral. This is a procedural development; the market has already priced it in. BTC is $63,094 (24h -0.09%), ETH is $1,881.7 (24h -0.16%), basically unchanged. The transmission path is clear: even if the SEC ultimately approves, the funds would push CME futures first, lifting futures prices. Arbitrage traders would then help close basis differences, indirectly transmitting to spot. That is not the same as a spot ETF directly buying coins. The chain is longer, so the force is weaker.
- Medium term: Slightly bullish. The SEC being willing to place 3x leveraged crypto products into the review queue is, in itself, a signal of regulatory loosening. When crypto is treated in parallel with commodities like gold and crude oil, and institutions have an even fuller toolbox, there are more options for future strategies.

My take

Watching from the sidelines; neutral in the short term. In plain terms, this is “accepted for review,” not “approved.” There are still comment periods and decision stages in between, so there’s considerable uncertainty. It’s unrealistic to expect this headline to pump the market. BTC is ranging around $63,094, and ETH is sitting around $1,881.7. This type of procedural news can’t change the near-term structure; the real catalyst would be either the approval landing or spot-ETF capital flowing back again. In the medium term, I’m logging this as part of regulatory normalization—slow-moving, not a breakout trigger. Also, 3x leverage is a double-edged sword: volatility amplification never amplifies only returns.

SEC officially starts reviewing 6x3 leveraged ETFs: BTC and ETH are just two of them
Previously, Cboe only filed the application—now the plot has moved forward by one step.
The SEC has officially issued a review notice covering six products: 3x gold, 3x silver, 3x BTC, 3x ETH, 3x crude oil, and 3x natural gas ETFs, and has begun soliciting public comments.
One-sentence translation:
Wall Street now wants to put the “3x daily leverage” into both crypto and commodities at the same time, and the SEC has begun deciding whether to open this door at all.
The two most important words here are still: daily.
These ETFs target three times the underlying’s daily price moves—not the idea that returns are multiplied by 3 forever. The fund mainly rebalances positions every day using instruments such as futures.
What’s really interesting is the regulator’s stance.
The SEC has previously raised concerns about risk for new ETFs with leverage above 2x. And in June this year, it specifically sought public comment again regarding “novel ETFs” related to leverage, options, crypto, and more.
So this isn’t a routine ETF approval.
If the final outcome allows 3x BTC/ETH, what may truly get opened is an entire batch of even more aggressive leveraged products.
At the moment, it’s entering a formal review—not already approved.

ECB investigation of 8,205 companies: only 0.2% accept crypto payments online, yet cash still accounts for 92%

💡 Negative: EU merchants accepting crypto payments online are only 0.2%—official data douses the crypto payment narrative with cold water

The European Central Bank has led a payments survey covering 8,205 businesses across the EU. The results are quite striking: only 0.2% of merchants are willing to accept cryptocurrencies online, and offline brick-and-mortar stores are just 1%. In the same period, 92% of physical merchants accept cash. Cash remains the most widely accepted payment method in Europe—by far. Even though crypto market value has surged several times over these years, in Europe’s day-to-day business, coins are still basically an observer. This data comes from the ECB’s cash usage study. The sample size is large and the source is official, so even those with multiple arguments find it hard to refute.

One sentence translation: Paying with crypto in Europe is still a niche thing. After all these years of the payment story, implementation has barely moved.

Market impact
Short term: This is a real blow to the “crypto payments adoption” narrative. BTC is currently around $63,054.34, largely flat (only 0.10% over 24 hours). The market doesn’t seem to be taking it seriously for now, but the bears now have an official stamp of approval. Once broader market sentiment weakens, this kind of data will be pulled out and amplified immediately. As for ETH $1,881.45, don’t even mention it—its payment narrative being dealt a setback won’t do less damage than BTC.

Mid term: The ECB has never been friendly toward crypto, and this report will further reinforce the official line that “crypto is a speculative asset, not a payment tool.” Going forward, EU funds will likely keep flowing toward CBDCs and traditional payment infrastructure, forcing industry narratives to shrink further to only “digital gold” as the remaining leg to stand on.

My view
Short term: Bearish, and I’m not being vague about this. Adoption-rate data isn’t formed in a single day, nor can it be digested in a single day—it will keep dragging down valuation logic. Whether BTC can hold the sideways range around $63,054.34 is a key observation point. If it breaks down, this negative news will shift from the backdrop into a catalyst. ETH $1,881.45 is already weak and has worse downside resilience. Here’s a risk point: if ETF fund inflows keep net-positive, macro positives could outweigh this type of adoption-rate negative—don’t be stubborn and assume the same story will always play out.

欧洲央行牵头搞了个覆盖全欧盟8205家企业的支付调查，结果挺扎眼：线上愿意收加密货币的商家只有0.2%，线下实体店也就1%。同期92%的实体商家接受现金，现金依然是欧洲接受度最高的支付方式，没有之一。虽然这几年加密市值翻了几轮，但在欧洲的日常生意里，币基本还是个旁观者。这份数据出自ECB的现金使用研究，样本量大、来源官方，多头想反驳都难下嘴。

According to publicly available quotes, the index closed at 7,798.99 points, up about 0.65% from the previous trading day. The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 0.13% to close at 53,839.99 points. The Nasdaq Composite rose 0.81% to close at 26,803.03 points. The Nasdaq 100 index also returned to above the 30,000 level after more than a month.

In terms of volatility, the S&P 500 volatility index briefly fell to a lower level within the year, indicating that short-term risk appetite has recovered.

Looking at the event backdrop, the index had already reached a phase high in early August, and this intraday breakout further heightened market attention to the broader U.S. stock market’s trajectory. In terms of market structure, heavyweight stocks generally moved higher. Multiple leaders across sectors such as technology and semiconductors recorded gains to varying degrees, providing support for the index’s advance. At the same time, sector differentiation was fairly clear: storage-related directions performed strongly, and most large tech stocks also moved up. By contrast, resources and some cyclical and defensive-related assets faced relatively more pressure. International gold prices and oil prices fell in tandem, suggesting that capital appeared to be reallocating between growth sectors and cyclical/defensive assets. Chinese concept stocks overall were weaker, indicating that the strength in overseas technology stocks and the performance of some cross-border assets are not perfectly synchronized.

On the core facts, the key catalyst was the U.S. July producer price index (PPI) released before the open. Total PPI rose 4.7% year over year, below the prior figure and market expectations. Core PPI rose 4.2% year over year. After the inflation readings eased, U.S. Treasury yields declined, and the market’s pricing of the policy path was adjusted accordingly, with traders becoming more likely to expect that the Federal Reserve will keep rates unchanged in September. It must be distinguished that this reflects pricing changes after the data release, not necessarily a shift in monetary policy. Communication within the Fed still shows public divergence, so subsequent interpretations remain uncertain.

In terms of the logic breakdown, this round of index highs is closer to a visible transmission chain: marginal easing of inflation pressure leads to revisions in rate expectations, which improves risk appetite for growth stocks; on top of that, the ongoing discussion about the artificial intelligence industry chain’s impact on earnings and capital expenditure adds further momentum. The activity in the storage sector is linked to market discussion about artificial intelligence expanding from training to inference, thereby increasing demand for storage infrastructure. In addition, the medium- to long-term financial models and shareholder payout plans published by some companies have reinforced short-term sentiment. However, whether high earnings guidance can be delivered and whether new business models can smooth out the cycle remains to be seen in subsequent earnings reports and order confirmations. What can currently be confirmed is the index level, closing performance, and the factual gains and losses across sectors; it cannot be directly extrapolated into an irreversible trend.

For the impact on the crypto market, it is mainly reflected in an indirect mapping from macro risk appetite and liquidity expectations, rather than a one-to-one linkage. When traditional risk assets strengthen due to easing data, institutions’ risk budgets and cross-asset allocation sentiment often warm up in parallel, which may boost high-volatility digital assets through channels such as expectations for U.S. dollar liquidity and “risk-asset resonance” that create a sentiment tailwind. If inflation reappears or officials turn more hawkish, valuations could be pressured again. It is important to be clear: new highs in U.S. stocks do not necessarily mean crypto assets will inevitably move up in tandem. Correlation between the two can change across different phases, and the crypto market is also constrained by multiple factors, including regulatory developments, supply-and-demand structure, and its own liquidity.

The editorial view holds that the S&P 500’s first intraday move above 7,800 and its refresh of a historical high indicate that—under data-driven conditions—the market is again testing the upside space. However, the close was still slightly below the integer level, showing that there is still a contest at key levels. Key items to watch next include the continuity of inflation and employment data, the consistency of policy communication, and whether technology bellwethers can deliver on earnings. For participants in the crypto market, it is generally more appropriate to treat macro events like this as a gauge of risk appetite—separating the already verified price levels and data facts from speculation about policy paths and the strength of cross-market transmission—so as to avoid extrapolating emotionally.

标普500盘中首破7800点刷新历史高位

当地时间8月13日，美股交易时段内，标普500指数盘中持续走高，首次突破7800点整数关口，并刷新该指数历史纪录。公开行情显示，指数收盘报7798.99点，较前一交易日上涨约0.65%；道琼斯工业平均指数上涨0.13%，收于53839.99点；纳斯达克综合指数上涨0.81%，收于26803.03点。纳斯达克100指数也在时隔一个多月后重返30000点上方。波动率方面，标普500波动率指数盘中一度回落至年内较低水平，显示短期风险偏好有所回升。

从事件背景看，该指数在8月初已触及阶段性高点，本次盘中突破进一步抬升市场对美股大盘走势的关注。盘面结构上，权重股普遍呈现上涨态势，科技、半导体等多个赛道龙头录得不同程度涨幅，为指数上行提供支撑。与此同时，板块分化较为明显：存储相关方向表现突出，大型科技股多数走高；资源与部分周期、避险相关资产则相对承压，国际金价与油价同步走低，资金在成长板块与周期、避险资产之间出现再配置特征。中概股整体偏弱，说明外盘科技走强与部分跨境资产表现并不完全同步。

核心事实层面，盘前公布的美国7月生产者物价指数是重要催化剂。整体PPI同比上涨4.7%，低于前值与市场预期，核心PPI同比上涨4.2%。通胀读数缓和后，美债收益率下行，市场对政策路径的定价随之调整，交易员对9月维持利率不变的概率有所上升。必须区分的是，这属于数据发布后的定价变化，并不等于货币政策已经转向，美联储内部沟通仍存在公开分歧，后续解读仍有不确定性。

逻辑拆解上，本轮指数新高更接近一条可见的传导链：通胀压力边际缓释，利率预期修正，成长股风险偏好回升，再叠加人工智能产业链对盈利与资本开支的持续讨论。存储板块的活跃，与市场关于人工智能从训练向推理扩展、从而提升存储基础设施需求的讨论相关；部分公司发布的中长期财务模型与股东回报安排，也强化了短期情绪。但高盈利指引能否兑现、新商业模式能否平滑周期，仍有待后续财报与订单验证。目前能够确认的是指数点位、收盘表现与板块涨跌事实，不能直接外推为趋势已不可逆。

对加密市场的影响，主要体现在宏观风险偏好与流动性预期的间接映射，而非一对一联动。当传统风险资产因数据缓和而走强时，机构风险预算与跨资产配置情绪往往同步升温，可能通过美元流动性预期、风险资产共振等路径，对高波动数字资产形成氛围层面的带动；若后续通胀反复或官员表态转鹰，则可能重新压制估值。需要明确：美股创新高本身不等于加密资产必然跟涨，两者相关性会随阶段变化，加密市场还受到监管进展、供需结构与自身流动性等多重因素约束。

编辑判断认为，标普500首次盘中站上7800点并刷新历史高位，说明在数据驱动下市场再度考验上方空间，但收盘仍略低于整数关口，显示关键位置仍有博弈。后续观察重点包括通胀与就业数据的连续性、政策沟通口径，以及科技龙头盈利兑现情况。对加密市场参与者而言，更宜把此类宏观事件视为风险偏好的温度计，把已核验的点位与数据事实，与政策路径、跨市场传导强度等推测分开看待，避免情绪化外推。

An official survey by the European Central Bank shows that EU businesses largely do not accept cryptocurrencies; the payment narrative has stalled, resulting in a negative sentiment backdrop.

The ECB surveyed 8,205 EU firms about payments—and the results are brutal: only 0.2% accept crypto payments online, and even in physical stores, the figure is just 1%. By contrast, 92% of merchants accept cash, and cash remains the absolute mainstream across Europe. This isn’t a small sample—these are official data covering the entire EU. In one sentence: while on-chain transfers may be all the rage, real-world payment scenarios barely exist.

Impact on the market
- Short term: Negative sentiment, but not fatal. BTC is stuck around $63,054 and ETH around $1,881 in a range without new narrative catalysts; this kind of data is likely to suppress any rebound strength, and funds will likely keep waiting.
- Medium term: Regulators now have official evidence suggesting “limited use.” Future European legislation is likely to be more cautious; for payment-token narratives, it will be hard to come up with a new story in the near term.

My view
Slightly bearish, but the impact is limited. The 0.2% figure does slap down claims about a “crypto payments year,” but with such a low base, there is still room for marginal improvement—don’t overinterpret a single survey. BTC is consolidating near $63,054: if it holds, it will keep grinding; if it breaks, more downside room will open. Risk point: surveys like this are naturally lagging and may underestimate the actual usage rate among younger users.

#dusk $DUSK @Dusk_Foundation  A couple days ago, bored out of my mind, I went and really dug into the testnet for @Dusk_Foundation . At first I thought this so-called “two-layer architecture” was nothing more than switching network ports with a wallet tweak. Turns out it wasn’t that shallow at all—I ended up burning almost two hours just to figure out the underlying logic.

This thing isn’t even remotely as simple as adding a toggle button on the front end. It’s two state machines that are basically incompatible with each other, sharing a single base. The public layer, Moonlight, follows the old route: it’s an account model like Ethereum, where the transaction flow is completely exposed, making it convenient for exchanges to look up accounts. Meanwhile the privacy layer, Phoenix, uses UTXO on top of PLONK zero-knowledge proofs, hiding transaction details tightly. These two “brothers” sit on the same consensus layer, but if you want to move an asset between them—say, using $DUSK  to “visit” the other side—you have to cross an extremely thick cryptographic barrier.

After browsing the official GitHub repos, the developers basically admitted it: cross-architecture transfers can’t be done in one step. In practice, coins you source from the public network are sent into the privacy layer, but at that point you’re forced through a “shield” step. Plainly put, it compels your device to locally hard-calculate a zero-knowledge credential, and the verification nodes only accept the codes—not the identity. After all these steps, the gas fee jumps to roughly three times that of a normal transfer. With the mainnet costing so much per inch, anyone using it for small-scale anonymous payments is basically handing themselves to fate. This isn’t because the product manager doesn’t understand user experience—it’s because the two hardcore underlying systems are fundamentally incompatible, and the resulting compute overhead can’t be avoided by anyone.

But don’t let this fool you: although this workflow is extremely discouraging for retail users, in the big narrative of RWA (real-world assets) it captures the attention of traditional financial giants perfectly. Wall Street institutions want to put things on-chain, but they’re worried about regulators scrutinizing them—and also worried that their cards will be exposed to competitors. The private securities on-chain project that Dusk teamed up with NPEX to pilot is a perfect example. The publicly visible Moonlight is there to handle audits and accounting checks, while the hidden Phoenix becomes a natural “dark pool” for big players to conceal highly strategic bids. Paying hefty fees for the safety of trade secrets is basically a no-lose deal for whales.

In the end, the current mechanism is honey for big players, but not very friendly to small retail users. The friction costs and waiting time caused by cross-layer back-and-forth are definitely a headache. #eth $ETH

这玩意儿压根不是前端加个切换键那么敷衍，而是两条水火不容的状态机在共用一个底座。公开层的 Moonlight 走老路子，跟以太坊一样是账户模型，流水全露在外面，方便交易所查户口；而隐私层的 Phoenix 玩的是 UTXO 叠加 PLONK 零知识证明，把交易细节捂得死死的。这俩兄弟虽然在同一个共识层上，但拿着 $DUSK 想串个门，必须得跨过一道极厚的密码学屏障。

翻了翻官方的 GitHub 库，开发人员也摊牌了：跨架构转移做不到一步到位。实操时，从公开网把水龙头领的币打进隐私层，被强行塞了一个“屏蔽（shield）”环节。说白了，就是逼着你的设备在本地硬算出一份零知识凭单，验证节点只认码不认人。这一套组合拳打下来，燃气费（Gas）直接飙到了普通转账的三倍！按主网那寸土寸金的消耗，谁拿它做小额匿名支付谁就是大冤种。这不是产品经理不懂用户体验，而是两套硬核底层互不兼容带来的算力损耗，谁也躲不开。

US states demand profit-sharing from AI data centers: this time, not an environmental fine—but a change to how profits are split

Multiple US states are pressuring AI data centers to share profits and disclose electricity pricing/accounting. As energy regulation tightens, BTC faces short-term headwinds.

Here’s what’s going on: In recent years, AI data centers have been expanding at a furious pace. Training large models is an energy-hungry business—some states’ power grids are close to being overwhelmed. As a result, local residents’ electricity bills have been rising. Now state lawmakers aren’t having it. They’re rolling out new rules: if you want to build and profit on my turf, you need to share part of your profits with the local area, and you also have to open up and itemize the electricity cost.

In simple terms: What used to be “tech companies get land and power as incentives for investment” is now being treated by states as a resource grab that needs to be regulated.

This is closely tied to the crypto market. US-listed mining companies have long been eyeing AI hosting opportunities—turning mining facilities into data centers to rent space to AI companies. That’s one of the toughest pieces of their valuation story. Now states are targeting the energy books of data centers, so the narrative of “mines become data rooms” will have to be questioned further, especially since mining is already viewed by states as another major electricity consumer.

Market impact
- Short term: The combined narrative of AI + mining is under pressure. Sentiment toward mining-company stocks cools, which can drag down crypto’s risk appetite. BTC is currently $63,072 moving sideways; if it can’t rise, it may seek support downward. ETH $1,881.9 is similarly weak, and any rebounds lack volume.
- Medium term: This is an energy accountability regulatory template. Today it targets AI data centers; tomorrow, the same logic can easily be applied to PoW mining. Once profit-sharing plus cost transparency becomes standard practice, miners’ profit margins may be structurally compressed, making it harder to tell the AI-transition story for publicly listed mining companies.

My view
I’m bearish in the short term. This news itself isn’t likely to blow the whole market up, but it changes expectations: the story line that AI would rescue miners has been disrupted by regulation. The narrative cooling is more damaging than the message itself. BTC trading sideways at $63,072 on lower volume is not a good sign; if it breaks down on expanding volume, the area below could turn into a vacuum. ETH is weaker too—whether $1,881.9 can be held depends on how far this regulatory sentiment plays out. We also need to be clear about the risk: if states’ final bills are watered down through lobbying into softer provisions, the downside may not meet expectations, and a rebound could arrive quickly.

#dusk $DUSK @Dusk_Foundation  Recently I personally ran through the @Dusk_Foundation  testnet and tried it end-to-end. I thought its “dual accounts” would be as simple as flipping an RPC in your wallet—turns out I spent half a day tinkering before I finally understood how it really works.

On the surface, Moonlight uses a standard account model: the ledger is fully transparent, making it convenient for exchanges to conduct background checks. In the shadows, however, Phoenix uses a UTXO + PLONK proof setup, tightly concealing both funds and counterparties. These two paths share the same consensus, but their underlying ledgers are fundamentally incompatible. To move $DUSK  across, you have to cross a thick wall of cryptography.

Even the official codebase admits that cross-layer transfers can’t be done in one shot. I tried moving test coins into the privacy layer, and the process forces an extra “shield” step—basically pushing you to compute a credential locally, while the node only verifies authenticity. After going through all that, fees immediately skyrocketed by three times. At mainnet pricing, using this for small anonymous transfers is absolutely doing charity. It’s not that the front-end UI is poorly designed; it’s that two accounting mechanisms are fighting each other, and the computational cost can’t be avoided.

That said, if you put this complicated machinery into the RWA track, it’s extremely appealing to big institutions. When tokenizing traditional assets on-chain, compliance often means exposing data—while privacy means it can’t pass audit. The private placement pilot Dusk and NPEX teamed up on plays the “both must be satisfied” game: regulators can inspect Moonlight’s transparent ledgers and public transaction flows, while large funds can hide in Phoenix’s dark pool to quote bids. For institutions, preserving trade secrets and paying a bridge fee to make the handoff is absolutely worth it.

But for regular players like us, constantly shuttling between the two layers is both expensive and time-consuming. If this is ever going to truly go mainstream, the only way is to rely on later batch routing and combine it with recursive aggregation proofs—packaging several cross-layer interactions into a single on-chain settlement. Only when Gas is driven down to near zero can everyone achieve truly “pain-free switching.” Until then, retail users are still safest staying put on the Moonlight side. #eth $ETH

AI isn’t a single big bubble—it’s a series of rolling bubbles: why the big crash is harder, yet the returns feel even more elusive?

Strategy analyst Joshi: AI isn’t a one-time bubble burst; it’s bubbles blown one after another—most of the money is likely to be burned.

Dhaval Joshi is a well-known strategist at BCA Research. This time, his view differs from the market’s “AI = Internet bubble 2.0” narrative. He believes AI won’t explode all at once like in 2000; instead, it will be a “rolling bubble.” First you hype chips, then data centers, then the application layer—when one theme deflates, the next one keeps propping up, while hot money rolls forward and pushes prices. The upside is there won’t be a one-day-style massive clearance crash. The downside is that each bubble cycle consumes real cash; once the tide goes out, you find out: you spent a lot, and long-term returns are a mystery.

One-line translation: AI won’t blow you up in one shot, but a dull-blade cut could be more brutal—capital is being mismatched cycle after cycle.

Impact on the market
- Short term: This statement itself is a bucket of cold water thrown on tech-sector sentiment. In crypto, the correlation with AI and tech stocks is extremely high right now. When the AI narrative cools off, small-cap alts have no story to tell, and BTC and ETH will also be dragged along by Nasdaq sentiment. BTC is stuck around $75.47,072.43, and ETH at $1,880.94—both in a lukewarm, neither-hot-nor-cold state. There’s no independent upside momentum; with just a gust of wind from outside, the market turns sideways and then drifts lower.
- Medium term: “Rolling bubbles” mean capital efficiency keeps deteriorating. Institutional money keeps burning in AI, and liquidity for the entire risk-asset complex gets misallocated and locked up. For crypto’s long-term incremental capital expectations, this is a negative—more like chronic blood loss than an acute bearish catalyst.

My take
To be honest, I’m on Joshi’s side—this bearish angle is far more grounded than the people who scream “collapse” every day. Cautious in the short run: BTC at $75.47,072 is a weak equilibrium. If the $75.47K integer level breaks and is lost, there won’t be very thick support underneath. ETH at $1,880 is even more fragile—funds haven’t truly flowed back. Cooling off in the AI sector is like adding fuel to the fire. The feature of rolling bubbles is that local rebounds can happen, but with each cycle the rebound’s strength and duration diminish. Don’t confuse a technical bounce with a trend reversal. Risks also need to be spelled out: the other side of rolling bubbles is that the narrative can be restarted again and again. In AI, another mega round of financing could reignite the story anytime—sentiment gets ignited at any moment. Chasing shorts is just as dangerous.

策略师Joshi：AI不是一个大泡沫，而是一个个轮着吹，钱大概率白烧。

Dhaval Joshi是BCA Research的知名策略师，这次的观点跟市面上“AI=互联网泡沫2.0”的论调不一样。他认为AI不会像2000年那样一次性爆掉，而是“滚动式泡沫”：先吹芯片，再吹数据中心，再吹应用层，一个主题泄了气，下一个接着顶上，热钱滚动往前推。好处是不会出现单日大崩盘式的出清，坏处是每一轮泡沫都在消耗真金白银，等潮水退了才发现：钱花了一堆，长期回报是个未知数。

一句话翻译：AI不会一下炸死你，但钝刀子割肉可能更狠，资本正在被一轮一轮错配。

对市场的影响
- 短期：这话本身就是给科技板块情绪泼冷水。币圈现在跟AI、科技股的联动性极高，AI叙事一降温，山寨没故事可讲，BTC和ETH也会被纳指情绪拖着走。BTC卡在$75.47,072.43，ETH在$1,880.94，都是不温不火的状态，没有独立上涨动力，外面风一吹，横盘就变阴跌。
- 中期：滚动泡沫意味着资金效率持续下降，机构钱持续烧在AI里，整个风险资产的流动性都被错配锁死。这对币圈的长期增量资金预期是减分项，不是急性利空，是慢性放血。

我的判断
说实话我站Joshi这边，这种看空角度比天天喊崩盘的实在多了。短期偏谨慎：BTC在$75.47,072属于弱平衡，$75.47K整数关口要是丢了，下方没有太厚的承接；ETH的$1,880更虚，资金一直没有真正回流，AI板块降温等于雪上加霜。滚动泡沫的特点是局部反弹会有，但每一轮反弹的力度和持续时间都在衰减，别把技术性反弹当趋势反转。风险点也要说清楚：滚动泡沫的另一面是叙事可以反复重启，AI那边再来一个超大额融资的故事，情绪随时被点着，追空一样危险。

What’s going on

This Ukrainian naval strike targets Russia’s “Bastion” coastal defense missile system located in Crimea. The system is a mainstay of the Russian coastal defense; it can both attack ships and strike targets on land—making it a high-value military asset. If Ukraine can precisely take it out, it shows that Ukraine’s strike capability into Crimea’s deeper areas has genuinely improved, and Russia’s strategic space is being compressed step by step.

In one sentence: the war hasn’t cooled down—it’s being doubled down toward the most sensitive direction, Crimea.

To put it simply, this has nothing to do with the crypto industry on the surface, but it affects the market’s overall risk appetite. Once the “geopolitical gunpowder” smell gets strong, money runs first—especially BTC, which trades 24/7 and has high liquidity. It’s always among the first assets to be sold.

Market impact

- Short term: A textbook “risk-off” trade. Capital rotates from risk assets into gold, the US dollar, and US Treasuries. BTC and ETH are hit first. Right now BTC $63,072.43 is up only 0.20% over 24h—it's already sitting on weak equilibrium—so this kind of news provides a ready-made excuse for a sell-off. ETH $1,880.94 is up 0.19%, momentum is also mediocre; when risk-off sentiment kicks in, it’s easier for it to underperform further.
- Medium term: If the Crimea direction keeps escalating, energy prices and inflation expectations will be pushed higher; rate-cut expectations would be delayed. That effectively keeps “siphoning liquidity” from the crypto market, which relies on liquidity. If the conflict drags on, tighter regulatory narratives may also increase—so don’t expect loosenings in the short run.

My take

Bearish in the short term, but not a collapse. BTC $63,072.43 is hovering right at the 63K psychological level; this is the most fragile spot. A little risk-off sentiment could push it down first. Whether 63K can hold is the key focus for the next 12 hours. ETH $1,880.94 remains below 1,900, showing even more weakness. My stance: moderately bearish and watchful over the next 12 hours.

Geopolitical news tends to come fast and fade fast. If Russia escalates in retaliation, the drawdown could be amplified. If there’s no follow-up, the “sentiment-driven” sell-off hole tends to get repaired quickly too. Don’t treat a single headline as a trend reversal, but also don’t assume there’s no geopolitical risk.

$SOL  SOLANA ETFs — Why Are They Important?

You’ve probably heard a lot about Solana ETFs, but what exactly are they, and why does the crypto market care? 👇

🔹 What is a Solana ETF?

An ETF (Exchange-Traded Fund) is an investment product that trades on a traditional stock exchange.

A Solana ETF gives investors exposure to SOL through a regulated financial product instead of requiring them to directly hold SOL in a crypto wallet.

In simple words:

Traditional investor → buys SOL ETF → ETF provides exposure to Solana

🚀 Why are Solana ETFs important?

1️⃣ Easier access

Investors who already use traditional brokerage accounts can gain SOL exposure through an ETF structure instead of managing a crypto wallet themselves.

2️⃣ Institutional interest

ETF products create another route for professional investors and financial institutions to gain exposure to SOL.

JPMorgan's latest filing, for example, disclosed a position in the Bitwise Solana Staking ETF, showing that institutional participation is expanding.

3️⃣ More visibility for Solana

ETF products can make SOL more accessible to traditional investors and potentially increase awareness of the Solana ecosystem.

4️⃣ Staking could be an important factor

Some Solana ETF structures include staking exposure, which is particularly interesting because SOL can generate staking rewards. However, the exact structure and fees differ between funds.

📊 What could ETF inflows mean for SOL?

If investors put significant money into Solana ETFs, the funds generally need exposure to SOL.

That can potentially create additional demand for SOL.

But remember:

ETF approval ≠ guaranteed price increase.

The price can still fall if the broader crypto market weakens, ETF demand is disappointing, or investors sell their positions.

⚠️ One important update

The Solana ETF story is not simply "waiting for approval" anymore.

Solana-linked ETF products have already entered the market, while issuers continue to introduce or modify products.

#dusk $DUSK @Dusk_Foundation  Imagine issuing a traditional bond worth as much as 100 million euros. Just piling up the due diligence reports, KYC files, and legal documents—there’s enough weight to overwhelm anyone. But here’s the twist: when this cumbersome process tries to interface with DuskVM, the system responds with a hard-and-fast order. The in/out data for a single contract call must be tightly constrained within a fixed 64KB argbuf space. Given all this large-scale institutional workflow, such a tiny capacity seems almost like a joke.

However, when you shift your perspective to end-to-end on-chain operations, these stringent limits actually look extremely smart. If you stuff massive amounts of text directly into the blockchain, not only would it burden every network node with heavy storage overhead, but once financial privacy is etched on-chain, it can’t be undone—fixing even a simple typo later becomes nearly impossible.

In reality, a distributed network doesn’t need to act like a “cloud drive.” The system only needs to verify three bottom lines: the original files have not been secretly replaced, the participants’ qualifications are fully compliant, and the subscription amounts haven’t gone out of bounds.

Once the mindset changes, the division of labor becomes clear. Those long, confidential contract drafts sit safely in authorized centralized servers; while on-chain, everything it does is limited to routing hash digests, compliance status, and zero-knowledge proofs. This 64KB isn’t a locked door meant to reject clients—it’s a forceful pushback mechanism. Don’t send fluff—just the receipts.

Of course, stripping out the data also means shifting responsibility. Once we understand how this works, we can be more objective about balancing the books for $DUSK . Don’t assume that because real money of 100 million euros comes in, token demand must surge proportionally. Static asset lockups don’t generate much value—the real consumption comes from high-frequency dynamic transfers.

Only when something changes in the network—identity refreshes, share splitting, profit distribution, or rule rewrites—will gas be genuinely burned. So the key metrics to watch going forward should be: for every million euros, how many on-chain interactions can be produced per year? And how much DUSK can be consumed as transaction fees? The narrow gate set by @Dusk_Foundation  is essentially digital discipline for the legitimate forces. As for whether this deal can truly run end-to-end, let’s keep observing how the data performs. #eth $ETH

只有当网络里发生身份刷新、份额切割、利润分发或者规则重写时，才会实打实地烧掉 Gas。所以，后续盯盘的核心指标应该变成：每百万欧元的资金，每年能折腾出多少笔链上交互？又能吃掉多少DUSK作为手续费？@Dusk_Foundation 设下的这道窄门，其实是在给正规军套上数字化纪律。至于这买卖究竟能不能跑通，咱们接着观察数据表现吧。#eth $ETH

But once this process reaches DuskVM, the system imposes a hard rule: for every contract interaction, the input/output can only go through a fixed 64KB argbuf channel. When I first saw that parameter, I was puzzled too—wasn’t Dusk aiming at traditional institutional finance? With such a paltry capacity, how could it possibly fit everything, let alone be enough?

But as you follow the full commercial loop, things suddenly click into place. If you copied the entire original text onto the blockchain, not only would node storage take a huge hit, but any privacy exposure would become a permanent headache, and typos would be impossible to fix. In reality, the network doesn’t care about the fine details of your terms. It only needs to verify a few core points: the materials are unaltered, the buyer meets the threshold, and the issued shares haven’t exceeded the limit.

So, leave the cumbersome contract in the traditional database, and on-chain just run hashes, status identifiers, and zero-knowledge proofs. This 64KB bottleneck is exactly what forces the project team to trim the excess—speak only in evidence.

Of course, with the heavy data kept off-chain, the burden shifts as well: who safeguards the drafts? If there’s a dispute ten years later, who provides the documents? Only once you think through that layer do you truly understand the setup’s hidden cards. The blockchain hasn’t uprooted “trust” entirely—it has condensed it into a few high-density verification checkpoints, and it requires them to stand up to scrutiny at any time.

Following this logic, the pricing model based on $DUSK  also needs to be reexamined. Even if a €100 million asset is fully registered on-chain, token purchase demand won’t simply inflate according to face value. The real consumption point is the subsequent dynamic operations: every time you verify identity, transfer shares, or distribute interest—that’s where real money burns as Gas.

If you’re planning to track it long-term, you’ll need to calculate carefully: for every million euros per year, how many on-chain interactions can you trigger? At this time last week, I was still staring blankly at the candlestick chart.
Now, flipping through a book instead, I suddenly understood one thing.

In Nassim Taleb’s book, The Black Swan, he says,
black swans can’t be predicted.
You can only make sure that
when it arrives, you’re still at the table.

Applied to trading, there’s just one rule:
Any single trade loss
must not take away your ability to keep trading.

Today, $ALLO  is at 0.2669,
up 3%.
Trading volume: 102 million USDT.
Looks pretty lively, right?
But this isn’t even close to the hair of a black swan.
For those with heavy positions,
a reversal of just 3% is enough to liquidate them.
So what are we talking about black swans?
For them, any little needle is a swan.

Being lightly positioned isn’t being timid—
it’s leaving yourself a way to stay alive.

#BTC #ETH #ALLO #投资哲学 #Trading mindset

Iranian tensions are heating up, but Gulf allies are rethinking their relationship with the United States: what exactly are they afraid of?

💡 Bearish factor: Gulf countries are reassessing their ties with the U.S. due to the ongoing situation with Iran. Geopolitical trust is weakening, and risk-off sentiment is suppressing risk assets.

What’s going on

Kyiv Post reports that Saudi Arabia and the UAE—America’s traditional Middle East allies—are re-evaluating their relationship with Washington. The spark is the continued intensification of tensions in Iran. In their minds, a question looms: are the U.S. security commitments truly reliable? Previously, the security architecture in the Middle East was essentially the U.S. acting as the bodyguard; now even the bodyguard’s own certainty is being called into question. As a result, these countries are starting to leave room for contingencies: diversifying diplomatic contacts, maintaining communication channels with Iran, and no longer putting all their eggs in the U.S. basket.

In one sentence: The U.S.’s Middle East allies are no longer betting on the U.S. unconditionally, and the regional security landscape is entering a period of re-shuffling.

Market impact

- Short term: Geopolitical uncertainty directly boosts risk-off sentiment. Just look at the chart: BTC is moving sideways at $63,064.1 (24h 0.00%), ETH $1,880.81 is stagnating on lower volume, and BNB is down 0.98%—showing that capital is already waiting. If news drops stating that “allies don’t trust the U.S.,” risk-off funds will only shrink further, and risk appetite will likely move lower. If oil prices react upward as a result, the stagflation narrative will be brought up again—adding double pressure on the crypto market.

- Medium term: If Gulf states truly start pulling away from the U.S., the dominance of U.S. dollar settlement in the Middle East will gradually be diluted. Ironically, this could be a long-term positive for non-dollar assets—but that’s something that plays out over years. The risks of conflict during the transition, oil price volatility, and sovereign wealth funds slowing their market entry are all headwinds for crypto. Don’t use long-term stories to comfort short-term positions.

My view

To be honest, I’m clearly bearish in the short term. BTC has been stuck at around $63,064.1 for such a long time, and when a geopolitical bearish shock hits during a sideways range, the market will most likely look for liquidity to the downside—that’s the direction with the least resistance. ETH $1,880.81 has weaker elasticity than the broader market to begin with, so the probability of it falling with the trend is even higher. Whether the $1,880 level can hold depends on how strongly this wave of sentiment takes hold. Scenario analysis: as long as there are no signs that Iran’s situation is cooling off, any rebounds are likely to be weak. If the situation escalates, don’t expect this time’s coin to act as “digital gold”—down first, think later. The risk is this: some people may package “de-dollarization in the Gulf” as a long-term positive. From a hindsight perspective, that narrative might be right—but it won’t save the next 24 hours’ price action.

怎么回事

Kyiv Post报道，沙特、阿联酋这批美国在中东的传统盟友，正在重新掂量和华盛顿的关系。导火索是伊朗局势持续紧张——盟友们心里犯嘀咕：美国的安全承诺到底还靠不靠得住？以前中东的安全架构基本是美国当保镖，现在保镖自己的确定性都在打问号。于是这些国家开始留后路：外交接触多元化、和伊朗保持沟通渠道、不再把鸡蛋全放美国篮子里。

一句话翻译：美国的中东盟友不再无条件押注美国，地区安全格局进入重新洗牌期。

对市场的影响

- 短期：地缘不确定性直接抬升避险情绪。你看盘面就懂：BTC在$63,064.1横着（24h 0.00%），ETH $1,880.81缩量趴窝，BNB还跌了0.98%，说明资金本来就在观望。这时候来一条“盟友都不信任美国”的消息，观望资金只会更缩，风险偏好往下走。如果油价因此起反应，滞胀叙事又会被拿出来讲，对币圈是双重压力。

- 中期：假设海湾国家真和美国拉开距离，中东的美元结算主导权会被慢慢稀释。讽刺的是，这对非美元资产可能算长期利好——但那是按年算的事。过程中的冲突风险、油价波动、主权资金放缓入场，对币圈全是逆风。别拿长线故事安慰短线的仓位。

#dusk $DUSK @Dusk_Foundation  Today, flipping through the latest document on @Dusk_Foundation , I was actually struck by the project side with a blunt, heartfelt line: “Tokenization can smooth out transfer and settlement frictions, but it can’t conjure real buyers, real sellers, and fair prices out of thin air.” In a circle that loves to paint grand promises, this kind of straightforwardness feels especially like fresh air.

Looking back at that long article from August 15 about the SME private placement market, Dusk stripped the division between on-chain and off-chain responsibilities down to the bone. Smart contracts handle everything from onboarding for eligible investors, to position bookkeeping, transfer restrictions, and settlement; but anything involving legal confirmation, sanctioned blacklist screening, notarization and custody, disputes and lawsuits—even the underlying funding requirements—has to be managed by the traditional “big brothers” offline to keep order.

To be fair, the fundamentals on the official site look quite impressive: the confirmed issuance size exceeds 300 million euros, it reaches more than 50,000 participants, and the amount of DUSK staked on-chain is also over 210 million tokens. The data is rich, but the stark reality is that Dusk Trade—the core hub that would truly activate these RWA into a trading bazaar—is still under construction, and neither DuskEVM nor Hedger has moved beyond the testnet.

So it means that the main suspense now isn’t about “how to issue tokens technically.” After the asset mapping comes the real test: who will pay for the stream of buy orders? What if there’s no market maker? Who will guard the fiat on-ramps and the underlying collateral? And if it really turns into an ownership labyrinth of “it depends,” should we put faith in that on-chain hash string, or should we wait patiently for court summons and the stamping from the registries?

If this whole system ends up being tightly bound to NPEX, traditional banks, custody giants, and regulators, then is it genuinely smashing the middlemen—or just needlessly adding yet another layer of complex network communication protocols?

I’m honestly quite impressed that the team directly states this time: “Tokenization does not equal liquidity.” Admitting that the hardest bones still haven’t been chewed through is far better than boasting that “going on-chain is everything.” Going forward, stop showing me more and more assets slated for上线. After the first batch of genuinely real, hard-assets goes live, the real test will be these hard metrics: actual daily trading volume, the position profile, and turnover rate—the fate of this whitepaper and the $DUSK  quality, finally laid bare. #eth $ETH

回顾 8 月 15 日那篇聊 SME 私募市场的长文，Dusk 把链上链下的分工剥得极度干净。智能合约包揽了合格投资者准入、持仓记账、流转限制以及结算；但凡涉及到司法确认、制裁黑名单、公证与托管、扯皮打官司，甚至底层的资金需求，统统得靠线下的传统老大哥们来镇场子。

不可否认，官网现在的基本面看着挺唬人：确认发行的体量超过 3 亿欧元，辐射 5 万多受众，网络里质押的 DUSK 也高达 2.1 亿枚以上。数据很丰满，但骨感的现实是，真正能把这些 RWA 盘活成交易集市的核心枢纽 Dusk Trade 还在施工，DuskEVM 和 Hedger 俩组件也没走出测试网。

这就意味着，现在的核心悬念早就不在“技术上如何发币”了。资产映射上来之后，才是真正的考验：连绵不断的买单谁来掏？做市商缺位怎么办？法币通道和底层抵押物谁来守？万一真遇上所有权罗生门，到底是去信链上那串哈希值，还是老老实实等法院传票和登记机构的盖章？

假如这一系列痛点到头来还是高度绑定 NPEX、传统银行、托管巨头和监管机构，那这套系统到底是真正砸碎了中间商，还是平白无故又垫了一层复杂的网络通信协议？

我其实挺佩服团队这次直接挑明“Tokenization 不等于流动性”。敢于承认最硬的骨头还没啃下来，总比吹嘘“上链即万能”强得多。往后看，别再给我秀又增加了多少待上线的标的物。第一批货真价实的资产开盘后，实打实的日成交额、持仓画像以及换手率，这几个硬指标，才是最终检验这份白皮书和 $DUSK 成色的生死状。#eth $ETH

#dusk $DUSK @Dusk_Foundation  Just finished reading the latest document disclosed by @Dusk_Foundation . What grabs your attention most isn’t deep, arcane ZK technology—it’s the official tone-setting line, said without any concealment: “Tokenization of assets can unblock transfer and settlement bottlenecks, but it can’t conjure buyers and sellers and fair pricing out of thin air.”

After spending enough time in this space, you’re used to all kinds of narratives that sell grand dreams. That kind of candor is genuinely rare. In the Aug 15 article exploring the SME private placement market, the project team lays out the line between ideal and reality very clearly. Smart contracts really can handle investor white lists, on-chain verification of rights, transfer controls, and settlement within seconds. However, once you’re dealing with real-world legal enforceability, anti–money laundering (AML) reviews, notarized custody, dispute arbitration, and—most importantly—actual investment demand, everything still has to rely on traditional financial institutions off-chain.

There’s no denying that Dusk’s current track record is solid: the issued asset size has confirmed to have surpassed the 300 million euro mark, the number of reached investors totals 50,000+, and the collateral pool has even locked in more than 210 million DUSK. The on-paper figures are impressive. But the core infrastructure that will determine whether these RWA assets can truly run a closed-loop business model—Dusk Trade—is still under construction, and both DuskEVM and Hedger are also only running on testnets.

So the key focus has already changed. People are no longer asking whether “real-world assets can be turned into Tokens.” Instead, they’re asking: after assets are on-chain, where do the ongoing buy orders come from? Who serves as the market maker to complete price discovery? Who underwrites the fiat on/off-ramp and who guarantees the underlying asset storage? The sharpest question is this: if ownership rights really end up tangled in disputes, do we truly believe “code is law,” or do we obediently defer to what local courts and registries decide?

If all of the hard-core pieces above ultimately still depend on NPEX, real banks, third-party custody, and traditional regulators, then we can’t help but ask: Is Dusk really revolutionarily cutting out intermediaries—or is it merely adding an even more complex network of on-chain coordination?

The good news is that the official is upfront in admitting that “Tokenization does not equal liquidity.” The only real yardstick is the actual daily trading volume, the current distribution of holdings, and the turnover rate—these are the sole standards for judging the quality of the whitepaper and the true value of $DUSK . #eth $ETH

在这个圈子待久了，听惯了各种画大饼的叙事，这种坦诚反而非常难得。在 8 月 15 日那篇探讨中小企业（SME）私募市场的文章里，项目方把理想与现实的楚河汉界划得很清晰。智能合约的确可以搞定投资者白名单、链上确权、流转控制以及秒级清算。然而，一旦涉及现实世界的法律效力、反洗钱审查、公证托管、纠纷仲裁乃至真实的投资需求，目前全得指望链下的传统金融实体。

不可否认，Dusk 目前交出的成绩单足够硬核：确认发行的资产规模突破了 3 亿欧元大关，触达的投资者数量达到 5 万+，质押池里更是锁定了超过 2.1 亿枚 DUSK。纸面数据非常豪华，但决定这些 RWA 资产能否真正跑通商业闭环的核心基建——Dusk Trade 还在建设中，DuskEVM 和 Hedger 同样只在测试网阶段运行。

因此，现在的核心考点早就变了。大家不再怀疑“能不能把现实资产做成 Token”，而是聚焦于：上了链以后，持续的买单从哪来？谁来充当做市商完成价格发现？法币通道以及底层资产存放由谁兜底？最尖锐的是，如果真的发生产权撕扯，到底是信奉“代码即法律”，还是老老实实听从地方法院和登记中心的发落？

假若上述这一系列硬核环节，最终仍要仰仗 NPEX、实体银行、第三方托管以及传统监管部门，那我们不禁要问：Dusk 到底是在革命性地砍掉中间商，还是徒增了一个更为复杂的链上协调网络？

好在，官方大方承认了“Tokenization 不等于流动性”，真实的日成交额、筹码分布状态以及换手率，才是检验白皮书成色以及 $DUSK 真正价值的唯一标准。#eth $ETH

On Sunday’s early trading hours, the market chose silence.

BTC was at $63,061, moving almost nowhere in 24 hours, -0.03%; ETH was at $1,881, a slight uptick of 0.09%. The numbers feel “quiet,” but quiet doesn’t mean safe.

━━━ Regime Assessment ━━━
The signals read by the Brahma System are crystal clear: BTC is currently in a bearish trend (BEAR_TREND), while ETH is ranging in a sideways consolidation (CHOP_MID). This isn’t bearish sentiment—it’s structural reality.
In a bearish trend, rebounds are, more often than not, traps; in a range, breakouts are, more often than not, fakeouts.

Most people are waiting for a “reversal signal,” while real traders are waiting for a “regime shift.” These are two completely different things.

━━━ Trading Psychology ━━━
Low volatility over the weekend most easily breeds greed—“The market is so steady; it’s a shame not to get in.” But steady conditions and safe conditions are not the same. Greed doesn’t only flare up during big spikes; it quietly plants itself in boredom.

━━━ Strategy Reference ━━━
Under the BTC BEAR_TREND regime, keeping position size light and waiting is preferred. If going short, wait for a pullback to confirm the structure. In ETH’s ranging setup, it’s a boundary tug-of-war—the middle should be avoided. If there’s no clear need to trade today, then don’t trade.

I’ve seen this kind of chart too many times. The hardest part isn’t finding opportunities—it’s doing nothing when there are no opportunities.

💡 Bearish catalyst: The UAE has been excluded from the Gulf defense system. With two risks stacking—ongoing Iran conflict plus infighting within the Gulf—risk assets are the first to get cut.

Background first: The Mecca Defense Pact is a Gulf defense alliance led on the Saudi side, aimed at coordinating to deter Iran. But the UAE, a major Gulf power, didn’t make the list.

With Iran’s situation still very tense around 2026, being left out isn’t just a matter of face. The UAE holds the port of Fujairah—outside the Strait of Hormuz, it’s the only large oil transshipment hub. Oil tankers from around the world rely on it to rotate and process flows. Excluding the UAE from defense coordination is essentially creating a major gap in convoy escort and air-defense arrangements on the south shore of the strait.

One-line translation: On the surface, it’s about unequal spoils; in reality, under the shadow of war, the Gulf is already splitting at the seams.

Market impact

In the short term, BTC is at $63,061 (24h -0.03%) and ETH at $1,881 (24h 0.01%), both flat—showing the market hasn’t priced this risk in at all. Roughly two-tenths of global oil passes through the Strait of Hormuz. The moment something changes there, oil prices jump first; inflation expectations then rise as well. The first things sold off are always risk assets. Crypto has carried a “high beta” label for years. When geopolitics heats up, it doesn’t get the safe-haven script—it gets the liquidity-drain script.

In the medium term: if the UAE and Saudi Arabia stay at odds for the long run, the risk appetite of Gulf sovereign wealth funds will shrink. This pool of money has been an important source of buy pressure in crypto over the past few years. Combined with higher geopolitical risk premia and capital flowing back into the US dollar and gold, the medium-term liquidity environment for crypto will be worse, not better.

My view

Bearish in the short term—no ambiguity. At $63,061, BTC is in a weak equilibrium, and even a single pinprick could break it. The longer this kind of sideways balance lasts, the uglier the breakdown becomes. For ETH at $1,881, liquidity is thinner, and historically when it falls, it falls harder than BTC. BTC drops 47% in a year, yet Strategy’s STRC rises 9%: why?

Bitcoin fell 47% over the past year, but Strategy’s preferred shares, STRC, are up 9% instead: funds are hiding in yield-bearing products, which is bearish for BTC spot.

The preferred share product issued by Strategy (formerly MicroStrategy), $STRC, climbed 9% against the trend over the past year. During the same period, BTC dropped 47%, and it’s currently quoted at $63,061.02.

The essence of this product is “crypto exposure with fixed coupon payments”: holders receive periodic distributions, not price upside. As a result, volatility is naturally lower than BTC’s. When BTC falls like this, it can still deliver positive returns—thanks to this layer of financial engineering.

In simple terms: institutional capital hasn’t left the Crypto space, but it no longer wants to directly withstand BTC’s price swings. They’d rather hold an interest-paying certificate. What the market “votes” for is cash flow, not price elasticity.

Impact on the market
- Short term: For BTC spot, this is a diversion rather than incremental demand. Money moves from a volatile asset into yield-bearing instruments, effectively signaling “we like the sector, but we don’t like the price.” BTC is at $63,061.02, moving only 0.03% over the last 24 hours—so sideways it can’t get any flatter. Such stalemates often come right before a big move. ETH is at $1,881.15, up 0.01% over 24 hours—no clear direction either.
- Medium term: Traditional finance is accelerating the securitization of Crypto. Coupon-bearing products and structured notes will keep proliferating. The upside is that entry becomes easier; the downside is that returns get skimmed by the middle layer, while on-chain spot gets sidelined. Regulators will likely “go along with it.” In the future, more capital will enter the market through securities channels rather than buying coins directly.

My take
I’m bearish. The reason is straightforward: an asset that’s down 47% in a year is being “voted for” with yield products around it—not by investing in the asset itself. That’s the classic case of confidence being split. BTC around $63,061 has already gone sideways to the limit: there isn’t enough upside incremental demand, while there’s selling pressure from profit-taking to the downside. Strategy (formerly MicroStrategy) issued only preferred shares, STRC. In essence, it’s a hybrid of “coupon/interest + equity.” Its volatility is far lower than MSTR’s common stock, and its returns are close to fixed income. Over the past year, BTC fell 47%, from today’s reference point $63,061.03; yet STRC is up 9%. Bearish on BTC in the short term. STRC’s rise against the market isn’t good news—it’s a bear-market picture: the most “safe” way for institutions to express themselves is “not betting on direction.” $63,061.03 is a near-term focus for both bulls and bears. Ukraine deploys British drones—battlefield upgrades are coming. Why is BTC still stuck at $63K?

💡 Negative factors: Western offensive weapons are entering the picture; the expected intensity of the Russia-Ukraine conflict rises → safe-haven capital flows back into the US dollar → BTC $63,054 faces short-term pressure.

British-made drones have officially joined the Ukraine battlefield. The key point is not the drones themselves, but the changed nature of Western military aid—from defensive equipment to strike capabilities that can shift the balance of the front lines. As a result, Ukraine’s control over the front and its negotiating leverage will also change. For Russia, once it’s been pushed into a corner, no one can guarantee how it will respond; uncertainty in European security has taken a step up.

In short: Western-provided weapons are becoming increasingly capable. This war may not be wrapped up in the short term, so the market needs to reprice geopolitical risk.

Impact on the market
- Short term: The transmission path is clear: escalation expectations → global risk appetite falls → capital first returns to the US dollar/US Treasuries as a safe haven → the crypto market absorbs the selling pressure. BTC $63,054 and ETH $1,880 trading in low-volume sideways action are, in part, digesting this backdrop of suppression. Geopolitical negatives usually don’t directly cause a sudden dump, but they sap buyers’ confidence; sideways drift lower is often more common than a crash.
- Medium term: With the fighting dragging on, European liquidity conditions remain under pressure. Expectations for energy price volatility may flare up again, uncertainty around the inflation path rises, and rate-cut timing could be pushed back. For the crypto market that relies on liquidity narratives, this is a slow-burn negative—worse over time than a short-term emotional shock.

My take
Honestly, I’m bearish in the short term. BTC has been grinding around $63,054 for so long, and the warming geopolitics provides an easy ready-made excuse for downside. ETH $1,880 is weaker; once that level is lost, the room for a pullback is larger than BTC’s. But geopolitical shocks are likely to be pulse-like—after sentiment has processed the impact, price action will return to its own rhythm. The hole you fall into when you dump, and the cautious opportunities later, are two different things. Don’t mix them together and get excited.
